summary: Suffered a sprained MCL on Aug. 18 during a joint practice with the Cowboys and did not appear in any preseason games; initial medical assessments pointed to 4-6 weeks out. As of Sept. 2, HC Kellen Moore said he's "not ready to rule out" Kamara for the Sept. 13 opener at Detroit but offered no guarantees, leaving him firmly in doubt.

With Alvin Kamara sidelined by a sprained MCL, Etienne is confirmed as New Orleans' starting running back for the foreseeable future; he already had the majority of first-team camp reps before the injury and now has the backfield to himself in the near term (Kendre Miller, Devin Neal, Ty Chandler behind him).

Placed on injured reserve Sept. 1 with an MCL sprain layered on top of a training-camp back injury, ruling him out at least four games. Signed by Detroit as a free agent this offseason to pair with Jahmyr Gibbs after the Lions traded David Montgomery to Houston, Pacheco now won't factor into the Lions' backfield for the start of the season at all.

Set for an even heavier early-season workload after backup Isiah Pacheco landed on IR (MCL sprain + back injury) on Sept. 1, leaving Detroit without its planned complementary back for at least the first four games.

Placed on injured reserve with a designation to return on Aug. 30 as he continues to deal with complications from the foot/ankle injury that ended his 2025 season in Week 3. He can't practice for at least two weeks and is ineligible to return before Week 5 against Detroit, so he opens the season off the 53-man roster entirely.

The No. 3 overall pick's high ankle sprain (suffered in the preseason opener) leaves him "about 50/50" for the Sept. 13 opener vs. the Chargers, per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo ("Nobody really knows right now"), even as HC Mike LaFleur says he's progressing well. With James Conner also opening the year on IR, a Love absence would push touches to Tyler Allgeier.

Now the healthier of Carolina's top two backs heading into Week 1 after missing most of August with a hamstring strain; HC Dave Canales says he "looks fast, strong, like he was before." With committee-mate Jonathon Brooks now dealing with his own issue, Hubbard projects as "a rock-solid fantasy starter" if Brooks can't go.

Working separately with trainers for close to a week with what HC Dave Canales called "soreness," putting his Week 1 availability in doubt just as he was set to reclaim a real role alongside Chuba Hubbard after back-to-back ACL tears. Canales says the team is taking it "one day at a time."

Aaron Jones holds the depth-chart edge on paper, but Mason out-efficienced him in 2025 (4.8 YPC to Jones' 4.2) and led him in red-zone work (15 carries to 10, 6 rushing TDs to 2) over the 11 games they shared. In their only joint preseason appearance the two split carries evenly (3 apiece), and one outlet projects "Mason should finish this game with more touches, even if Jones technically gets the start."

Retains the technical starting nod over Jordan Mason on Minnesota's depth chart, but the two split carries evenly in their lone shared preseason outing and multiple camp reporters give Mason the efficiency and red-zone edge — a genuine, volatile timeshare rather than a clear lead role for Jones.

HC Mike McCarthy said Sept. 7 he's "very pleased" with both Warren and free-agent addition Rico Dowdle, calling the pairing "awesome," and wants to deploy both across all three downs rather than a traditional starter/backup split. Warren is listed ahead of Dowdle on the official depth chart despite Dowdle taking a share of first-team reps throughout camp.

Splitting reps with Jaylen Warren throughout camp and into Week 1 prep; HC Mike McCarthy praised both backs' camps on Sept. 7 without committing to a touch split for the opener vs. Atlanta. A real committee rather than Dowdle clearly winning the job his 1,076-yard 2025 season in Carolina might suggest.

Listed as Seattle's RB1 on the team's first unofficial regular-season depth chart (Sept. 2), ahead of both 2026 first-round pick Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson, while Zach Charbonnet remains on PUP. The report itself calls the exact ordering "hair-splitting" since real carries are expected to be shared fairly evenly among all three.

Slotted second at RB on Seattle's Sept. 2 unofficial depth chart, behind George Holani rather than the clear-cut lead role earlier camp buzz suggested for the rookie first-rounder, with Zach Charbonnet still out on PUP (at least four games). A three-way committee with Holani and Emanuel Wilson looks likelier than a Price workhorse role early on.

Co-listed with Chris Rodriguez atop Jacksonville's depth chart with no clear separation; OC Grant Udinski said Sept. 4 the pair are beginning to "hit their groove" and he's encouraging both to "play freely, and let the game come to them." LeQuint Allen also siphons third-down work, muddying the picture further for Week 1.

Officially sits atop Houston's depth chart entering Week 1 and signed a two-year, $16.5M extension this offseason; one projection has the early-down/goal-line work split roughly 70/30 in his favor over Woody Marks despite the two running near-even reps through camp.

Projects as the passing-down complement behind newly-extended David Montgomery for Week 1 (roughly a 30% share in one estimate), a step down from the near-even committee reps he got throughout camp despite leading Houston in rushing as a rookie in 2025.

Waived by Dallas on Aug. 30 (cutdown day) despite flashing big-play ability in camp and preseason (94 rushing yards); Malik Davis won the RB2 job behind Javonte Williams instead on the strength of his own preseason production and special-teams value. Blue is now a free agent rather than the Cowboys' presumed backup.

Won the Cowboys' backup running back job behind Javonte Williams on cutdown day (Aug. 30), beating out Jaydon Blue (waived) on the strength of a strong preseason (68 yards on 12 carries, an 8-yard receiving TD) plus special-teams value.

Placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List on Aug. 31, three days after being formally charged with two misdemeanors (battery and criminal damage to property) stemming from a May incident with his girlfriend. He cannot practice, play, or be on the 53-man roster while the case proceeds (initial court appearance moved up to Sept. 10), though he is still paid; his attorneys call it an administrative step, "not a final determination."

Traded from Pittsburgh to Green Bay on Aug. 30 for a 2028 sixth-round pick, timed directly to the Josh Jacobs exempt-list news, giving the Packers a former third-round back as backfield insurance. Johnson was buried on Pittsburgh's depth chart as a rookie (69 yards on 28 carries) but now lands in a wide-open Packers room.

Heads Green Bay's post-cutdown depth chart with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List and Emanuel Wilson departed to Seattle in free agency; he navigated camp and preseason healthy for the first time in his career after prior ankle, groin, and hamstring issues limited him to one career game played. Kaleb Johnson (newly traded in) and Chris Brooks sit behind him.

Has not practiced since slipping and hurting his right ankle on Aug. 24; per ESPN's Mike Reiss (Sept. 6), unless he logs a limited practice soon he's "trending toward missing" the Sept. 9 opener at Seattle. New England already brought in Corey Kiner as RB3 insurance behind the top two.

Named the Patriots' "clear-cut starter" for Week 1 by ESPN's Mike Reiss (Sept. 6) with TreVeyon Henderson trending toward missing the opener with an ankle injury. Expected to handle an enlarged workload against a tough Seattle run defense, projecting as a high-end RB2 with Corey Kiner as the only real competition for the vacated touches.

Returned to practice Sept. 1 after a groin injury that had sidelined him for Washington's final two preseason games, putting him back on track for the Sept. 13 opener against Philadelphia and preserving his standing as the early-down piece of the Commanders' committee.

Made the Giants' initial 53-man roster and says he's on track to play Week 1 against Dallas as he continues recovering from his severe 2025 rookie-season ankle injury (dislocation, open tibia/fibula fracture, ligament damage). New HC John Harbaugh's run-heavy system should still get him meaningful touches even if his snap share is managed early, despite added depth (Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy, Devin Singletary) behind him.

Made New York's initial 53-man roster despite an uncertain path there — uneven preseason play, the offseason arrival of Najee Harris, and a neck injury suffered in the preseason finale all worked against him. With Skattebo, Harris, and Devin Singletary all healthy ahead of him, Tracy is hard-pressed for regular Week 1 touches even though he kept his roster spot.

Did not take part in on-field work during the media-access portion of the 49ers' first full practice in Melbourne on Sept. 6 ahead of the Week 1 game vs. the Rams; HC Kyle Shanahan declined to discuss specifics, citing the Australia trip's injury-report timing rules. No clear indication yet whether this is a new issue or scheduled rest, but it's the first hint of anything since he was fully healthy and back to regular drills.

Remains the Rams' nominal starter but his workload ceiling keeps shrinking — his carry share fell from 73.7% in 2024 to 55.7% in 2025 (51.4% over the final 11 games) — and per ESPN's Dan Graziano (Sept. 2), the team plans to push the split with Blake Corum "pretty close to 50-50" in 2026.

Set to see meaningfully more carries in 2026 after finishing 746 yards on 145 carries a year ago; per ESPN's Dan Graziano (Sept. 2), the Rams plan to bring the Kyren Williams/Corum split "pretty close to a 50-50 split" this season rather than the roughly 55/45 (Williams-favored) look of late 2025.

Faces no meaningful new competition for touches entering Week 1 vs. the Colts — Justice Hill returns as the change-of-pace back and Rasheen Ali is ticketed mainly for special teams/kick returns, while rookie Adam Randall (IR) won't factor in before Week 5. Henry averaged 19.6 touches and a touchdown per game over the prior two seasons and projects for a similar workhorse role.
